newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil seeks to stop disease after massive floods.
newsitem.headline: Brazil seeks to stop disease after massive floods.

text.p: Brazilian health authorities have launched a campaign to prevent outbreaks of disease in areas devastated by weekend flooding that killed more than 70 people and left 45,000 homeless, the Civil Defence said on Tuesday.

"The biggest danger is leptospirosis because cases have to be hospitalized or there is a risk of death," Civil Defence head Pedro Sanguinetti said, refering to a disease transmitted by rat urine that causes fever, jaundice and internal bleeding.

Sanguinetti said authorities were distributing medicine and disinfectant in areas hit by the flooding, where communities were also at risk from diarrhoea. Torrential rains lashed southeastern and central Brazil for 10 days in late December and early January but stopped on Tuesday, leaving about 180 towns and cities in three states under water.
The threat of disease from flooded sewers was heightened by the lack of drinking water and power.

In central Minas Gerais state, the worst hit by the flooding, where at least 71 people died, authorities began distributing medicine and disinfectants to communities affected by the disaster. Air force helicopters and planes were required to reach the most isolated groups.

Dozens of municipalities in Minas Gerais and neighbouring Rio de Janeiro and Espirito Santo states declared states of emergency and the federal government pledged it would help purchase food and medicine.
